items.name: Neural voice (Kokoro, English)
items.summary: More natural engineer voice that runs on your CPU - 12 English speakers, about 120 MB
items.description: Kokoro-82M v1.0 (int8) through sherpa-onnx: 12 English speakers, British and American, synthesised on the CPU with the same radio clicks, volume and pace settings as the Windows voices. One-off download; pick a neural voice under Settings > Voice once it is installed. Two licences travel with the pack: the Kokoro model is Apache 2.0, and the espeak-ng phonemiser data is GPL version 3 or later. Both texts and the notices are inside the download.
items.author: TrulyAsleep

news.title: Eight more languages, on the dev branch first
news.body: Russian, Polish, Dutch, Japanese, Chinese (Simplified), Korean, Czech and Hungarian are coming as drafts. Drivers on the DEV update branch can try them now in 0.5.4-dev.3, and everyone else gets them with 0.5.4.

news.title: Crash reports you can read before you send
news.body: If the app hit an error and closed, the next time you open it there is a card in Settings under CRASH REPORT holding the whole report. You read it, tick the box, press Send. What you see is exactly what gets sent, and nothing leaves this machine unless you press it.

news.title: F1 25, and the format your game is sending
news.body: A Game setting under GAME CONNECTION - F1 26 or F1 25. Picking F1 25 turns on the 2025 telemetry format, built from the published spec and covered by tests but never yet confirmed against the running game, so it is off unless you turn it on. The connection strip now names the format it is actually receiving.

news.title: ERS calls arrive where they are meant to
news.body: A call used to be decided the moment you reached the point it applied to, but speech takes about half a second to reach your ears - roughly fifty metres at racing speed - so you heard it after the corner. Calls now leave early enough to land in the right place, and in the right order.

news.title: The app no longer closes itself mid-race
news.body: The dashboard updates ten times a second on the same thread as the window, with no error handling around it, so one bad number anywhere in it ended the whole app instantly with nothing written down. It now survives that and writes down what happened instead.

news.title: Diagnostics stop recording names
news.body: The diagnostic file the app writes beside itself no longer holds your Discord account, this PC's join key or the other drivers on track. It keeps the same numbers, with the identities stripped out of the copy.

news.title: Sharing a strat works
news.body: Share this strat never reached the server - every share was refused and nothing was stored, so importing a code found nothing either. Both work now. Sharing hands you an eight-character code, and Import paints it onto the mode slot it was saved from, once you have confirmed the circuit and the slot.

news.title: Downloads page, and install from file
news.body: One place for the extras the app can fetch, the neural voice first. Every download is checked against a signed catalog before it installs, and Install from file takes the same package by hand, so an offline build gets the extras too.

news.title: Offline build
news.body: A second flavour of the app with the online features left out on purpose: no update checks, sign-in, XP, listings or strat sharing. Installs beside the full version with its own data folder.

news.title: Signed release files
news.body: Every release now ships a signed manifest. A copy whose files have been edited refuses to start, and the updater only installs a download whose signature checks out.

news.title: Neural engineer voice
news.body: A far more natural engineer that runs on your own CPU instead of the Windows voices. Download the voice pack once from Voice and Radio, about 120 MB, then pick one of the neural voices from the picker.

news.title: 0.3.0 released on GitHub
news.body: The first public release - installer and zip on the F1RaceEngineer-dist repo. Existing installs are offered it through Check for updates.

news.title: Radio that talks about your race
news.body: Pit-stop radio only for cars that can affect you, stuck-behind advice that knows your strategy, and the catch projection re-speaks when the picture changes. First-boot wizard for the port, voice and Discord.

news.title: Off-strategy stops tracked to the end
news.body: When a rival on a different strategy stops, the engineer follows it lap by lap: gap and trend, their lap time against yours, the running total, and a box-within-N-laps countdown when the undercut is live.

news.title: Voice toggles are real
news.body: Strategy switch alerts, Traffic and undercut warnings, Tyre cliff warning and ERS coaching each silence their own calls and remember your choice. Session recording follows the sessions with no cap.

news.title: Measured pit loss, endgame projector, recorder on
news.body: Pit-lane time loss is measured per circuit from every car that stops and used in every box call. One call when a rival on fresher rubber is going to catch you, and which lap. The flight recorder is on by default.

news.title: Safety car standing orders and the lap replay
news.body: When a VSC or SC comes out the engineer already knows whether to box, and says so once. Review Data replays a lap over the learned track with the rivals side table and battery at the cursor.

news.title: Lap review against your best
news.body: Difference any lap against your own best on the same circuit: delta trace, per-corner time won and lost, and stacked speed, ERS and gear traces. The app records the session so there is always something to review.

news.title: Track limits calls
news.body: Race control's own verdicts as radio: lap deleted, penalty, and where you ran wide, with the stringency setting read from the game. Repeat offenders at the same corner get told.
